topic: Eval dataset in KB S3 prefix poisons retrieval
question_text: A developer stores their Bedrock Evaluations dataset (eval-dataset.jsonl with question/answer pairs) in the docs/ prefix of their RAG S3 bucket. After uploading, the chatbot starts returning strange answers quoting expected answers verbatim. What happened?

options.text: The Knowledge Base ingested the evaluation file as source content — its question/answer pairs are now retrieved as context, poisoning real responses
The evaluation file corrupted the embedding model
The file exceeded the context window
The JSONL format is not supported by S3

explanation: Bedrock Knowledge Bases ingests all supported files in the configured S3 prefix. Placing the eval JSONL (full of Q&A pairs) in the same prefix used for the KB data source causes it to be chunked, embedded, and retrievable — contaminating real responses with verbatim expected answers. Fix: store eval datasets in a separate S3 prefix or bucket NOT linked to any data source.

topic: LLM-as-a-judge requires a stronger judge model
question_text: In Amazon Bedrock Evaluations, a team configures Claude Sonnet as the judge and Claude Haiku as the evaluated model. Why must the judge model be stronger (larger/more capable) than the model being evaluated?

options.text: A weaker judge cannot reliably assess quality beyond its own capability ceiling — its evaluations would be unreliable for the harder tasks the evaluated model handles
The judge model must be from a different provider than the evaluated model
AWS requires the judge to have a higher per-token cost
The judge needs more GPU memory to store both outputs simultaneously

explanation: A judge model must be more capable than the evaluated model to reliably score quality on complex tasks — a weaker model cannot recognize correctness beyond its own ability. There is no cross-provider requirement; cost is a consequence not a rule; and GPU memory is not a concern since evaluation runs as separate inference calls, not simultaneous in-memory comparison.
